text:
Noah: heads up — saw KV cache memory climbing steadily on H100 with long-context chat traces. doesn't happen on mi250x in the same workload.
Maya: oof. any logs? rough reproduction steps?
Noah: simple repro: single convo, 1k tokens prefix, then 30 requests that extend. attached run log:
```
kvcache: put_page idx=10240 gpu=0 tag=0x3 owner=0x7f8ff1 alloc_ts=3076543201
kvcache: migrate_page idx=10240 -> gpu=1 tag=0x1
kvcache: page_table: found entry owner=0x7f8ff1 tag=0x3 != hw_tag=0x1 (mismatch)
rt_event: evict_worker stalled 120ms
```
Noah: looks like tag/owner mismatch after cross-gpu migration, then the page isn't freed and keeps being referenced.
Raj: that line "tag != hw_tag" rings a bell. similar to a historic tiled-remap race but this is different cause it's post-migrate. which driver and runtime?
Noah: CUDA 12.3 on H100, ROCm 5.7 on mi250x. runtime build: kvcache opt+sanity (no heavy debug).
Liang: can you dump `kvcache debug dump_pt idx=10240` and `nvprof`/nsys stack for the evict path? I want to see sequence numbers.
Noah: dumping now, pasted snippet:
```
PT[10240]: state=VALID tags=[0x3] hw_tags=[0x1] refcnt=2 last_writer=serve0 seq=8773
EvictQ: enqueued page idx=10240 owner=serve0 reason=shadow_mismatch
```
Noah: refcnt never goes to 0, evict retries because hw tag mismatches and we re-migrate repeatedly -> leak/growth.
Maya: does this only happen when NVLINK is present? any difference with single-GPU runs?
Noah: single-GPU run doesn't trigger it. NVLINK + cross-GPU migration seems required. Also only reproducible under high concurrency (batching enabled).
Raj: hypothesis: migration scheduler coalesces pages then applies a partial remap that updates hw_tag but not shadow tag atomically, race with in-flight writer increments refcnt. eviction sees inconsistent tags.
Eva: +1 for a race. quick mitigation: disable cross-gpu coalesced migrations (set KVCACHE_MIGRATE_COALESCE=0) and disable batching on that worker, see if it stops.
Noah: confirmed: crash run with env tweak stops growth. batch size 8 -> growth, batch size 1 -> no growth.
Liang: please run a debug build with atomic remap asserts enabled: `make runtime DEBUG_KV_ATOMIC_REMAP=1` and repro under the same workload. also collect `nvlink` counters and `nvidia-smi dmon`.
Maya: sounds like a good bisect target. can you test @tagged-tiling branch? (we had an earlier change that added per-page tags during tiling).
Noah: tried tagged-tiling off, still see mismatch but rarer. When tagged-tiling on + coalesce on -> high prob.
InfraBot: deploy-bot: created job 3076543245 to run longtest-kvcache-h100 on canary pool.
Raj: if this is a non-atomic two-step update (hw_tag then shadow_tag), we need to either make the update atomic or quiesce writers. atomic update will be tricky for hybrid GPU architectures.
Liang: patch idea: add a write-intent bit to page meta before migration, consumers check intent bit and wait or retry. less invasive than full atomic remap.
Eva: note perf tradeoff — extra intent-check on hot path could regress 1-2% latency. but prevents growth and long-term OOMs.
Maya: agreed. prioritize safety for now. can we gate intent checks behind `KVCACHE_SAFE_MIGRATION=1` config per-deployment?
Noah: I'll prototype intent-bit approach and run the canary job. also attach `nsys` timeline, shows concurrent write on same PFN while migrate does remap: screenshot + timeline id 8721.
Liang: if prototype passes, we should add microbench: cold mem, steady-state longctx 4k tokens, and stress cross-gpu NVLINK at 80% load. capture alloc/free histograms.
Noah: initial prototype pushed to `noah/kv-migrate-intent` PR: https://git.internal/redwood/kv/1234
Maya: nice. add tests: 1) single-GPU no-regress, 2) multi-GPU repro (fails before, passes after), 3) race-fuzzer that toggles coalesce.
Noah: test results from canary (job 3076543245): PASS under intent-bit prototype, zero growth after 10k reqs. posting artifacts.
Raj: great. follow-up: we should also audit rocm path — ensure similar atomicity semantics on mi250x (even if it wasn't failing there, ensure correctness).
Eva: schedule a short sync tomorrow 10am to decide rollout plan and perf hang. I'll draft a release note. :white_check_mark:
Noah: thanks all — will iterate on microbench numbers and open a rollout RFC once we have perf stats.
Maya: cool, please @here when RFC is ready.
